sentences.text:
This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with FIR No.39/2023 registered at Police Station Mandawa,
District Udaipur, for offences under Sections 450, 376(2)(N)(F), 506 IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Drawing attention of the Court towards FIR, charge-sheet and the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., learned counsel submitted that as per prosecutrix she was subjected to sexual assault by the petitioner on 21.4.2023 at the point of knife when she was sleeping in her house with her four children.

Learned counsel submitted that it is highly improbable that the prosecutrix who is aged about 35 years would not shout or seek help of her children, who were sleeping in the very same (2 of 3) [CRLMB-10129/2023] house at the time, she was being subjected to sexual assault by the present petitioner.
Learned counsel submitted that during investigation, the police has not recovered any knife allegedly used by the petitioner for commission of alleged crime.
Learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact, the petitioner and family members of the prosecutrix are having strained relations, owing to some land dispute between them.
It was further submitted that there is no apprehension of petitioner influencing any of the prosecution witnesses or tampering with any of the evidence.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that for the alleged incident of 21.4.2023, the FIR had been lodged by the prosecutrix on 27.4.2023 without any plausible explanation for the delay.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody, challan has been filed and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that it is highly improbable that the prosecutrix, who is a mature married woman would not shout or cry for help when she was subjected to sexual assault particularly when her four children were sleeping in the very same house at the time of commission of alleged crime.

(3 of 3) [CRLMB-10129/2023] Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case,
this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

Accordingly, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Malaram S/o Bhuraram shall be enlarged on bail in connection with FIR No.39/2023 registered at Police Station Mandawa, District Udaipur, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to so.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.
